_about: Every word the analysis page shows about the case, the law and the loan, in plain operator language. Each entry restates the legal meaning in DECOMPOSITION.md (§1 map, §3 chains, §4 questions); it never changes what the model does. Figures in braces are filled from the run's data.

situation.title: Akoustis Technologies · 20 Jun 2024
lines: Akoustis makes radio-frequency filter chips. It asks Slope to pay its supplier invoices and repays each one in three monthly installments.

On 20 May a federal jury verdict became a $38.6M judgment against Akoustis in favour of Qorvo, a competitor, for taking trade secrets and infringing patents. Akoustis says that is more than its liquid assets. It has about {cash} of cash.

The judge has not yet ruled on Akoustis's challenges to the verdict. Meanwhile Qorvo can start collecting, $44M of Akoustis's notes can come due early if the judgment stays unpaid, and Nasdaq may delist the stock.
situation.question: What does this do to Slope's credit line through {horizon}?
situation.line: Slope's line: limit {limit} (15% of monthly receipts, Slope's published rule), a 3.7% fee per invoice, each invoice repaid in 3 monthly installments. Slope pays a new invoice only while the balance fits under the limit, nothing is overdue and Akoustis has not filed for bankruptcy.
situation.bank_note: Bank data is reconstructed from Akoustis's reported figures; the account data itself is private.

futures.sub: Each square is 1% of modeled outcomes.
futures.headline: Filing probability

funded.label: Funded
funded.note: Invoices Slope paid under the line through {horizon}.

due.label: Due by {horizon}
due.note: Installments falling due by {horizon}. Installments of later invoices fall due after it.

unpaid.label: Due, uncollected
unpaid.note: Past due, or owed when Akoustis files.

stuck.label: Balance at filing
stuck.note: Expected balance Akoustis owes Slope on the day it files, across all outcomes (zero where it doesn't file). Recovery depends on the bankruptcy and falls after {horizon}.

clawback.label: Preference exposure
clawback.note: Collections in the 90 days before a filing, which a bankruptcy trustee can seek to recover. Gross, before defenses. It falls with the research because Slope collects less in the run-up to a filing.

why_lower: The line stops funding once an installment is past due or Akoustis files. With the research, that can happen from August rather than late November, so Slope funds less, and more of what it lent is owed at a filing.

jev.name: Jev
jev.intro: Jev is a forecasting model. For each decision, it reads the court and SEC record and gives the probability of one party's next move. Code sets every date and amount and combines the probabilities along each path.
jev.question: Question
jev.drag: Drag to override; every figure on the page updates.

ts_liability_jmol.short: Judge throws out the trade‑secret verdict
ts_liability_jmol.question: Does the judge throw out the trade-secret verdict?
ts_liability_jmol.why: If yes, the $31.3M award, the $7.0M punitive award, the fees and the interest all fall away.

ts_damages_ruling.short: Judge keeps, cuts or retries the $31.3M
ts_damages_ruling.question: Does the judge keep the $31.3M trade-secret award, cut it, or order a new trial on damages?
ts_damages_ruling.why: A cut leaves about $23.1M, if Qorvo accepts it. A new trial means no trade-secret money is owed before 17 Dec.

remittitur_accepted.question: If the judge cuts the award, does Qorvo accept the lower amount instead of a new trial?
remittitur_accepted.why: Accepting fixes the award at about $23.1M. Refusing means a new trial, with no trade-secret money owed before 17 Dec.

patent_jmol.short: Judge throws out the patent verdict
patent_jmol.question: Does the judge throw out the $280k patent verdict?
patent_jmol.why: Small next to the trade-secret award.

trebling.question: Does the judge triple the trade-secret damages, as Qorvo asks, under North Carolina's unfair-trade-practices law?
trebling.why: Tripling would raise the amount owed to about $94M; the $7.0M punitive award then drops out. The jury answered no on that question, which weighs against it.

fees_awarded.short: Judge orders Akoustis to pay Qorvo's legal fees
fees_awarded.question: Does the judge order Akoustis to pay Qorvo's $12.1M of legal fees?

appeal.question: Does Akoustis appeal within 30 days of the final judgment?
appeal.why: An appeal alone does not stop Qorvo collecting; only a court-approved pause does. It does delay when Qorvo can reach cash in other states.

execute_pre_ruling.question: Does Qorvo start collecting the judgment now, before the judge rules on Akoustis's challenges?
execute_pre_ruling.why: The judgment has been collectable since 20 Jun. Akoustis's operating cash sits outside Delaware, so Qorvo reaches it only once the judgment is final, or earlier if the judge allows it.

registration_early.short: Judge lets Qorvo reach Akoustis's cash early
registration_early.question: Does the judge let Qorvo collect from Akoustis's accounts in other states before the judgment is final?
registration_early.why: If yes, Qorvo can seize Akoustis's cash without waiting for the appeal deadline.

enforce_after_final.short: Qorvo moves to collect after the ruling
enforce_after_final.question: After the ruling, does Qorvo move to collect what's owed?
enforce_after_final.why: A seizure takes whatever cash Qorvo can reach, whatever Akoustis needs to operate.

stay_motion.short: Akoustis asks the judge to pause collection
stay_motion.question: Does Akoustis ask the judge to pause Qorvo's collection?
stay_motion.why: A pause normally needs a bond for the full judgment plus interest. Akoustis cannot fund that, so it offers the cash it has beyond a month of operating costs.

stay_approved.short: Judge pauses collection on less than a full bond
stay_approved.question: Does the judge pause Qorvo's collection on the smaller security Akoustis can offer?
stay_approved.why: Judges can accept less than a full bond for good cause. If yes, Qorvo cannot seize cash, but the security Akoustis posts is locked up.

debtor_response.question: When Qorvo moves to seize cash, what does Akoustis do: seek a buyer or new financing, file for bankruptcy, or neither?
debtor_response.why: Seeking a buyer or financing delays the decision to the next point of pressure. The record gives no terms, so no new cash is counted.

settlement_offer.question: Does Akoustis offer Qorvo a settlement?
settlement_offer.why: The offer is what Akoustis could actually pay: its cash beyond a month of operating costs ({offer} before the ruling). A settlement ends Qorvo's collection and the noteholders' judgment default.

settlement_accept.question: Does Qorvo accept Akoustis's settlement offer?
settlement_accept.why: Paying the settlement takes cash out of Akoustis at once, but removes the judgment's threat.

holders_act_judgment.question: Do the noteholders declare a default on the unpaid judgment and demand their $44M now?
holders_act_judgment.why: The notes let holders of a quarter of them do this once a judgment over $10M has gone unpaid and unpaused for 60 days. When that clock starts is open under the notes' wording: 19 Aug counting from the judgment as entered, or 60 days after the judge's ruling. The model carries both.

holders_act_delisting.question: If Nasdaq delists the stock, do the noteholders demand all $44M now, make Akoustis buy back their notes, or neither?
holders_act_delisting.why: Delisting is a default under the notes and gives holders the right to be bought out in cash.

petition_on_notes.short: Akoustis files for bankruptcy once the notes are due
petition_on_notes.question: Once the noteholders demand repayment it cannot make, does Akoustis file for bankruptcy?

holders_involuntary.question: If Akoustis doesn't file, do three or more noteholders force it into bankruptcy?
holders_involuntary.why: Under the notes' terms, no earlier than 60 days after they demand repayment. Qorvo cannot do this alone.

reverse_split_board.question: Does Akoustis's board call a shareholder vote on a reverse stock split in time to lift the share price above $1 by Nasdaq's 21 Oct deadline?
reverse_split_board.why: Without it, the stock stays under Nasdaq's $1 minimum and faces delisting.

split_approved.question: Do shareholders approve the reverse split?
split_approved.why: Approval keeps the listing; delisting is a default under the notes.

nasdaq_hearing.short: Akoustis asks Nasdaq for a hearing
nasdaq_hearing.question: If Akoustis misses the 21 Oct deadline, does it ask Nasdaq for a hearing?
nasdaq_hearing.why: A hearing request holds off the suspension while the panel decides.

panel_exception.question: Does Nasdaq's hearing panel give Akoustis more time, keeping the stock listed through 17 Dec?
panel_exception.why: If no, the stock is delisted.

petition_cash_floor.short: Akoustis files for bankruptcy when cash gets tight
petition_cash_floor.question: When Akoustis's cash first falls below what it needs to run for the next month, does it file for bankruptcy?
petition_cash_floor.why: The same question is asked on bank data alone and with the research, at the day and cash level each path reaches.

petition_cash_out.short: Akoustis files for bankruptcy when cash runs out
petition_cash_out.question: If it keeps going, does Akoustis file for bankruptcy when its cash runs out?
petition_cash_out.why: Asked only where it did not file when cash first got tight.
